source.label: Wikipedia: Huizong, a painter, poet and calligrapher, reigned until the Jin conquest of 1126
Waley: Huizong “was chiefly famous for his realistic pictures of birds and flowers”
Palace Museum record: 芙蓉锦鸡图轴 (hanging scroll)
Wikipedia lists Huizong as a representative of gongbi bird-and-flower painting

work.text: As a painter Hui Tsung was chiefly famous for his realistic pictures of birds and flowers. “In painting birds he gave them eyes of lacquer the size of a bean, which stood out in relief,” says Teng Ch'un, writing about 1180 A.D.

source.author: Arthur Waley
source.title: An Introduction to the Study of Chinese Painting

moment.text: Once some of them were called in to paint a pheasant walking in the garden. They made wonderful pictures, rich in colour and striking in their naturalness ; but the emperor said that they all were wrong. … when a pheasant is climbing a rockery, it does not lift the right foot first (as represented in their pictures) but the left.
moment.lead: Osvald Sirén, retelling an anecdote of the emperor and his Academy painters:

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

matters.text: He was the supreme authority in all matters relating to art and took an active part, for instance, in selecting subjects for the examinations and in criticizing and correcting the works of the painters.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II
